snippet: Stanford Researchers Create AI Agents with Memory, Reflection, and Planning | Yash Khandelwal posted on the topic | LinkedIn # Stanford Researchers Create AI Agents with Memory, Reflection, and Planning 𝑳𝒊𝒗𝒊𝒏𝒈, 𝒃𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒅𝒊𝒈𝒊𝒕𝒂𝒍 𝒗𝒊𝒍𝒍𝒂𝒈𝒆𝒔 𝒂𝒓𝒆 𝒏𝒐 𝒍𝒐𝒏𝒈𝒆𝒓 𝒔𝒄𝒊𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒆 𝒇𝒊𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏. 🏠 I read a paper today that just amazed me on what kind of things people are doing using AI. If you don't have time for the full read, I highly recommend at least checking out the abstract to see how they brought a digital village to life. https://lnkd.in/dQkKb36d This research was conducted by researchers from Stanford University and Google, and they even built a startup called Simile, securing $100 million in funding with some of the top AI visionaries like Andrej Karpathy among the investors. 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐩𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭? Researchers created "Generative Agents", AI characters that live in a virtual town called Smallville. Unlike NPCs (non-player characters) in traditional video games like 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘚𝘪𝘮𝘴 that follow a script, these agents are powered by large language models and possess: - 𝑨 𝒎𝒆𝒎𝒐𝒓𝒚 𝒔𝒕𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒎: They record everything they experience in natural language. - 𝑹𝒆𝒇𝒍𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏: They don't just store data; they sit back and think about the memories to form high-level beliefs about their world and themselves. - 𝑷𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒏𝒊𝒏𝒈: They create long-term plans like hosting a Valentine's Day party and dynamically adjusting them based on what other agents do. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐡𝐚 𝐌𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 💡: In the simulation, the researcher saw emergent social behaviors. One agent was told she wanted to host a party. Without further human intervention, she invited friends who then told other friends. They coordinated their schedule, and on the day of the event they all showed up at the right place and time to socialize. 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞? - 𝑰𝒎𝒎𝒆𝒓𝒔𝒊𝒗𝒆 𝒘𝒐𝒓𝒍𝒅𝒔: Imagine video games or training simulation where every character has a unique soul, memory, and evolving relationship with you. - 𝑺𝒐𝒄𝒊𝒂𝒍 𝑷𝒓𝒐𝒕𝒐𝒕𝒚𝒑𝒊𝒏𝒈: Testing how a new policy or a viral piece of information might spread through a community before it's released in the real world. - 𝑷𝒆𝒓𝒔𝒐𝒏𝒂𝒍 𝑨𝒔𝒔𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒏𝒄𝒆: Moving from simple chatbots to agents that truly understand your history, preference, and long-term goals. The bridge between human behavior and computational simulation is narrowing. This is the blueprint of the next generation of human-AI interaction. #ai #agents "human- ? Or are ?
